results.title: Cape Coast targets global tourism status with new investment drive
results.content: Cape Coast Mayor in the Central Region, George Justice Arthur, says the assembly is seeking to position the historic city as a global tourism destination through increased investment in hospitality, cultural enterprises and digital tourism services.

results.title: Cape Coast Mayor calls for stronger links between tourism and agribusiness
results.content: The Mayor of Cape Coast Metropolis in the Central Region, George Justice Arthur, has called for stronger partnerships between tourism businesses and local farmers, fishers and food processors to ensure that tourism spending generates more income and jobs for local communities.

results.title: Obuasi SHTS abuse: Expert demands sex offenders register, child protection reforms
results.content: Communication, gender and safeguarding expert Mercy Catherine Adjabeng has called for a public sex offenders register, independent investigations into sexual abuse allegations, and an end to the quiet transfer of teachers accused of sexual misconduct, demanding a sweeping overhaul of Ghana’s child protection system.

results.title: Miracles Aboagye criticises Veep over silence on alleged sexual abuse at Obuasi SHTS
results.content: New Patriotic Party (NPP) Director of Communications, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has criticised Vice-President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang for not publicly commenting on allegations of sexual misconduct involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai.

results.title: NAIMOS destroys 92 chanfang machines in four days on Tano River
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says it has destroyed 92 chanfang machines in four days during operations against illegal mining on the Tano River at Asemkrom in the Aowin District of the Western North Region.

results.title: 19-year-old woman remanded over alleged stabbing death of 33-year-old boyfriend at Ofankor
results.content: The Tesano Divisional Police Command is investigating the death of 33-year-old Enoch Abrokwa, who allegedly died after being stabbed by his 19-year-old girlfriend, Emmanuella Asante, at Ofankor Barrier in Accra.

results.title: GH¢24.8bn paid to statutory funds on time and in full — Ato Forson
results.content: According to him, the payments reflect a departure from the delays, capping and arrears that previously affected the release of statutory funds.

results.title: Let the law take its course in Obuasi SHTS abuse exposé – Vice-President Opoku-Agyemang
results.content: Vice-President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has called for the law to take its course in the sexual assault case involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), describing the matter as a serious national concern with implications for both present and future generations.

results.title: Parliamentary Human Rights Committee urges CID, Attorney-General to expedite Obuasi SHTS abuse case
results.content: The Parliamentary Committee on Human Rights has called on the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) and the Attorney-General to expedite investigations and prosecutorial processes into allegations of sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS).

results.title: Macroprudential assessment shows systemic vulnerabilities within banking industry remain subdued – BoG
results.content: According to the Bank of Ghana, the macro-financial risks remained contained on account of favourable macroeconomic conditions, declining sovereign risk perceptions, and strengthening investor confidence, thereby diminishing the risk of capital flight.

results.title: Size of Ghana’s economy to hit $128bn, maintaining 8th largest economy in Africa
results.content: This means the size of the Ghanaian economy will take a quantum leap from the earlier $114.71 billion.

results.title: Ghana calls for UN reforms to give Africa greater voice in global decisions
results.content: Ghana has called for a more representative, responsive and effective United Nations (UN), urging reforms to ensure Africa’s priorities are better reflected in global decision-making.

results.title: Education Minister acted promptly on Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations – Hashmin Mohammed
results.content: Spokesperson to the Education Minister, Hashmin Mohammed, has defended Haruna Iddrisu’s handling of the alleged sexual abuse at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), insisting that the Minister took prompt steps to facilitate investigations into the matter.

results.title: Bethel Revival Choir announces Akpe Experience 2026
results.content: Bethel Revival Choir has announced the 2026 edition of its annual praise and worship concert, Akpe Experience, themed “Faithful God” and inspired by Lamentations 3:22–23.

results.title: Imperial Global Ghana, UK High Commission lead drive for science Journalism in Ghana
results.content: Thirty Ghanaian journalists have received training in emerging technologies under the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technologies Fellowship, an initiative by Imperial Global and the British High Commission in Ghana to strengthen science journalism. The programme, now in its fourth year, forms part of the UK-Ghana Science, Technology and Innovation (ST&I) Strategy, which seeks to deepen cooperation between the two countries and improve public understanding of scientific developments. The training equipped participants with practical skills and knowledge in artificial intelligence (AI), climate change, digital tools and other emerging technologies.

results.title: Chief Moomen partners Africa Arts Network for ‘Nkrumah Showboy’
results.content: Bambu Heritage Productions and Africa Arts Network (AAN) have signed a Master Cooperation Agreement to collaborate on theatre productions, cultural advocacy and infrastructure development, with plans to stage Nkrumah Showboy in 2027.

results.title: YEA plans four new employment programmes for 2027 – Basintale
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) is planning four new employment programmes for 2027 as it seeks to expand opportunities for young Ghanaians in domestic services, delivery, corporate services and agriculture.

results.title: December in Ghana must deliver economic benefits beyond entertainment – Tourism Minister
results.content: The Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, has called for the annual December in Ghana festivities to deliver tangible economic benefits for Ghanaians beyond entertainment. Speaking at the launch of December in Ghana 2026 on October 20, she said the celebrations must create jobs, support local businesses and provide sustainable livelihoods for people working in the tourism and creative industries. “The true value of December in Ghana must be measured not only by the excitement of the events or the number of visitors it attracts, but also by the sustainable economic opportunities it creates for Ghanaians,” she said.

results.title: Mamprugu Traditional Council sues Jamong royals over rival chief’s enskinment in Bunkpurugu
results.content: The Overlord of the Mamprugu Traditional Area, Naa Bohagu Abdulai Mahami Sheriga, has filed an application at the High Court in Nalerigu seeking to have four people committed for contempt of court over the enskinment of a rival chief for Bunkpurugu in the North East Region.

results.title: YEA considering amendment of Act to become Ghana’s main employment corridor – Basintale
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) is considering an amendment to its enabling law to position the institution as Ghana’s main corridor for employment opportunities, Chief Executive Officer Malik Basintale has announced.

results.title: YEA says it receives no allocation from District Assemblies Common Fund
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) says it continues to receive no allocation from the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), despite a provision in law for funding from the source.

results.title: 6th iNTTA opens in Cape Coast with focus on Ghana’s 24-hour economy
results.content: The sixth edition of the Inter Tourism Expo Accra (iNTTA) has opened at the Ridge Royal Hotel in Cape Coast, bringing together investors, policymakers, entrepreneurs and tourism industry players to explore investment opportunities in Ghana and across Africa.

results.title: Sammy Ayeh picks NDC nomination forms to contest Deputy National Communications Officer position
results.content: Governance Spokesperson at the Presidency, Dr Sammy Ayeh, has picked nomination forms to contest for the position of Deputy National Communications Officer of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC).

results.title: Obuasi SHTS closure leaves final-year students facing uncertainty ahead of WASSCE
results.content: The academic future of final-year and second-year students of Obuasi Senior High and Technical School (SHTS) remains uncertain, as the school has stayed closed to continuing students for nearly three months following a student riot in August. The school was shut down on August 5 after the municipal assembly ordered its closure following a disturbance in which students reportedly attacked the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, amid allegations of sexual abuse involving female students. Despite the start of the new academic calendar for senior high schools, academic activities at Obuasi SHTS have yet to resume for continuing students.

results.title: YEA calls for review of Communication Service Tax funding cap
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) is calling for a review of the funding cap affecting revenue from the Communication Service Tax (CST), arguing that the arrangement has implications for the resources available to implement its employment programmes.

results.title: Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations: Education Ministry knew nothing until exposé – Dr. Apaak
results.content: The Ministry of Education has said it knew nothing about the alleged sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) until an investigative documentary by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni was brought to its attention.

results.title: All 1,000 Northshore Garment Project beneficiaries have secured jobs – YEA
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) says all 1,000 young people recruited under its Northshore Garment Project have secured employment, with plans to enrol another 1,000 beneficiaries under the initiative in 2027.

results.title: YEA targets 11,200 beneficiaries under US$3.6m AfDB-backed programme
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) is preparing to train and create employment opportunities for 11,200 beneficiaries under the Ghana Women and Youth Employment and Social Cohesion Programme (GWYESCO), with approximately US$3.6 million earmarked for the Agency.

results.title: YEA secures overseas jobs for more than 1,000 beneficiaries under Labour Exchange Programme
results.content: More than 1,000 beneficiaries of the Youth Employment Agency (YEA) have so far accessed employment opportunities in different countries under its Labour Exchange Programme, Chief Executive Officer Malik Basintale has announced.

results.title: YEA increases monthly beneficiary allowances to GH¢800 – Basintale
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) has increased monthly allowances for its beneficiaries from GH¢500 to GH¢800, representing a 60% increment, Chief Executive Officer Malik Basintale has announced.

results.title: YEA secures 60% retention agreements with security agencies – Basintale
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) says it has secured retention agreements with security agencies to facilitate the absorption of at least 60% of beneficiaries after completing their two-year engagement period.

results.title: YEA recruits 100,628 beneficiaries, achieves 75.7% of 2026 target
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) has recruited 100,628 beneficiaries as of September 30, 2026, representing 75.7% of its annual target of 133,000, Chief Executive Officer Malik Basintale has announced.

results.title: ‘Probably our funniest film yet’ – Shirley Frimpong-Manso on ‘Agency for the Dead’
results.content: Film producer Shirley Frimpong-Manso is promising audiences plenty of laughter with Agency for the Dead, describing the ghost-themed production as potentially the funniest film her team has made.

results.title: YEA partners Ghana Digital Centre to train 2,000 young people in IT
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ghana Digital Centre to enrol 2,000 young people in information technology-related programmes and capacity-building initiatives.

results.title: GIS arrests 34-year-old foreign national; others on the run for human trafficking
results.content: The Savannah Regional Command of the Ghana Immigration Service, led by Deputy Commissioner of Immigration, Lawrence Agyei Agyapong, has busted a 34-year-old Nigerian national known as Prince James, a.k.a. Prince Odogunu, for alleged human trafficking in Clooth, an illegal mining community in the Bole District of the Savannah Region.

results.title: How was a teacher facing sexual misconduct allegations promoted to headmaster? – Sarpong Asiedu questions GES
results.content: A Democracy and Development Fellow in Public Health at CDD-Ghana, Kwame Sarpong Asiedu, has questioned the circumstances under which the headmaster at the centre of the Obuasi Senior High Technical School sexual abuse allegations was appointed, amid claims of earlier misconduct.

results.title: Monrovia set for AWBL Zone 3 qualifying showdown
results.content: With the competition set for the Samuel Kanyon Doe (SKD) Indoor Gymnasium in Paynesville, the participating teams face a demanding week in which every result could prove decisive in their quest to reach the continental finals in Cairo, Egypt, scheduled for December 11–19.

results.title: YEA to deploy 6,000 community teaching assistants by November – Basintale
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) plans to onboard and deploy 6,000 community teaching assistants by the end of November 2026 under an agreement with the Ghana Education Service (GES).

results.title: Black Bombers arrive in Kinshasa for 2026 IBA Africa Elite Boxing Championships
results.content: Ghana’s Black Bombers have arrived in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, ahead of the 2026 IBA Africa Elite Men’s and Women’s Boxing Championships. The competition, scheduled to run from October 19 to November 1, will provide the national team with an opportunity to test its readiness against some of the continent’s best boxers. Ghana […]

results.title: Who protects the dreamer? (Part II) — Reflections on the vulnerability of the Girl Child in the Obuasi Senior High Technical School Scandal
results.content: There is something sickeningly cruel about a society that encourages a girl to dream, sends her to school to build that dream, and then leaves her vulnerable to the very people entrusted with protecting her. The allegations emerging from Obuasi Senior High Technical School against its headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, involving sexual abuse, including rape, are deeply disturbing. If established, these allegations would represent not merely a crime, but a monstrous betrayal of trust, authority and the sacred responsibility of educating children.

results.title: Obuasi SHTS students remain at home nearly 3 months after closure over headmaster’s sexual abuse claims
results.content: The academic fate of many final-year and second-year students of Obuasi Senior High and Technical School remains uncertain as the school has been closed indefinitely to continuing students for nearly three months now.

results.title: ‘Don’t treat it as an Obuasi episode’ – Kofi Asare calls for school safeguarding reforms
results.content: The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch, Kofi Asare, has called on the Ghana Education Service (GES), the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Gender to use the sexual abuse scandal at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) as an opportunity to reform safeguarding systems across the country.

results.title: Trump and Zelensky appear at loggerheads despite new optimism
results.content: The hug that Trump envoy Steve Witkoff offered Volodymyr Zelensky before talks in Oslo is unlikely to have dispelled the Ukrainian leader's misgivings about the current direction of US policy towards his war-ravaged country.

results.title: YEA trades and vocational programme exceeds 2026 target by 73% – Basintale
results.content: The Youth Employment Agency’s trades and vocational programme has recorded 51,900 beneficiaries against an annual target of 30,000, exceeding its target by 73%, Chief Executive Officer Malik Basintale has announced.

results.title: DVLA warns public against fake SMS payment links and online fine scams
results.content: The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) has warned the public against fraudulent text messages and online payment links used by scammers to collect money from unsuspecting motorists under the pretext of paying fines.

results.title: Stop! Go! Stop Again! The NDC’S three-day course in political principles (Updated)
results.content: Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, there lived a traffic policeman whose understanding of road safety depended entirely on which vehicle was approaching.

results.title: From Potential to Practice: Africa’s AI decade has begun
results.content: A month after PAAIS 2026, the summit's convenor reflects on what the room revealed and what leaders in boardrooms and ministries must do now.

results.title: Finance Ministry to meet maritime stakeholders over Tema Port clearance delays
results.content: The Ministry of Finance will meet key stakeholders in Ghana’s maritime and logistics sectors on Wednesday, October 21, to discuss proposed changes to customs clearance procedures amid concerns about persistent delays and rising costs at Tema Port.

results.title: NDPC DG urges action on existing policies to boost Ghana’s human capital
results.content: The Director-General of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Dr Audrey Smock Amoah, has called on stakeholders to focus on implementing existing policies and commitments to build a productive human capital ecosystem in Ghana.

results.title: NDPC boss urges greater use of evaluation evidence in national development planning
results.content: The Director-General of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Dr Audrey Smock Amoah, has called for greater use of evaluation evidence in national development planning to improve policy implementation, resource allocation and accountability.
